hook: Flies spot a predator wasp by its long antennae. A handful of neurons steer the defense.
hook_turn: A handful of neurons steer the defense.
summary: Flies kick and swat in directions set by where a parasitoid wasp appears, triggered mainly by the wasp's elongated antennae. Genetic manipulation and activity recordings traced this to a few visual neuron types that feed LC9, which combines antenna and body signals before passing the wasp's location to motor circuits. The work is in flies and a single predator, so the general mechanism is a proposal.
title: Visual object recognition in the fly: the internal representation of a predator drives defensive behaviour
